sentences.text: Hello, and welcome to the Slow English Podcast.
Today we will talk about South Africa.
South Africa is a large, beautiful, and diverse country at the southern tip of Africa.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Are you ready?
Let's begin.
Where is South Africa?
South Africa is in the south of the African continent.
It borders Namibia, Botswana, Zimbabwe, Mozambique, and Eswatini.
It also surrounds a small country called Lesotho.
South Africa has two oceans, the Atlantic Ocean in the west, the Indian Ocean in the east.
What is the capital city of South Africa?
South Africa has three capital cities.
Pretoria for government, Cape Town for Parliament, Blomfontine for the courts.
The biggest city is Johannesburg, a modern city with business and culture.
Cape Town is famous for Table Mountain and the Sea.
How many people live in South Africa?
About 60 million people live in South Africa.
It is a multicultural country with many languages, ethnic groups, and traditions.
People call it the rainbow nation.
What language do people speak in South Africa?
South Africa has 11 official languages.
The most common are Zulu, Sosa, Africans, English, Sisotho.
Most people speak more than one language.
English is used in schools, business, and government.
What is the weather like in South Africa?
South Africa has many climates.
In general, it is sunny and mild.
Summers are warm, November to March.
Winters are cool and dry, made to August.
The coast is mild and the inland areas are hot in summer and cold in winter.
What does South Africa look like?
South Africa has many landscapes.
Mountains, like the Dreykensburg grasslands, called the Heivelle Deserts, like the Carou
beaches along two oceans.
National parks with wild animals.
It is one of the most beautiful countries in the world.
What animals live in South Africa?
South Africa is famous for wildlife.
In game reserves and national parks, you can see the Big Five, Lion Elephant, Leopard
Rhino, Buffalo.
There are also giraffes, zebras, and hippos, crocodiles, monkeys, and penguins.
Yes, penguins.
Many types of birds and insects.
What do people eat in South Africa?
South African food is varied and delicious.
It mixes African, Dutch, Indian, and British influences.
Popular foods include pap, a soft porridge made from maize corn, bry, a barbecue with meat,
bunny chow, spicy curry inside bread, bobo de spice meat with egg topping, vet coke,
fried dough bread, chakalaka, a spicy vegetable mix.
Meals often include meat, vegetables, and sauce.
What do people drink in South Africa?
People drink water.
Tea, especially robust tea, a red herbal tea, coffee fruit juice.
Adults may drink beer or South African wine.
South Africa is famous for its wineries.
What is life like in South Africa?
Life in South Africa is different in cities and villages.
In cities, people work in offices, go to school and drive cars.
In rural areas, people may farm, raise animals, and live in close communities.
People enjoy music and dance, watching soccer, rugby, or cricket, going to church or family
gatherings, nature trips and bries, barbecues.
What are some holidays and traditions in South Africa?
Freedom Day, April 27, celebrates the end of apartheid, Heritage Day.
September 24 celebrates all cultures, Youth Day, June 16, Christmas, New Year's and Easter.
Local festivals with music, food, and art.
People wear traditional clothes, sing, and celebrate diversity.
Some fun facts about South Africa.
South Africa has three capitals.
The flag has six colors, very unique.
The cradle of humankind is in South Africa, where early human fossils were found.
Nelson Mandela was the country's first black president.
South Africa has 11 official languages, more than any other country.
Now you know many things about South Africa.
You know where it is, what people speak, and what they eat.
You learned about the weather, animals, holidays, and daily life.
Well done.
I am Emili.
Goodbye.
Or as they say in Zulu, Humbakahle.
